attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post. 'I believe' introduces a firm opinion, not a graded probability.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps the $50B revenue scale, the trillion-dollar framing and the media's role. 'Roughly' fairly reflects a rounded figure. It is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Using Q2 2025 annualised revenue, a separate revenue boundary and a metaphorical reading of 'masquerading' is an ordinary, fair plain reading. The result still depends on market-boundary and accounting choices the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: Menlo's own $12B consumer AI spending estimate. It covers only part of the market and is a company disclosure, so it cannot set the industry-wide total.
March 2025 coverage of Gartner's $644B spending forecast, mostly hardware. It is spending, not revenue, it falls outside Q2, and one article cannot show media-wide amplification.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no market-wide Q2 2025 annualised generative AI revenue estimate with stated coverage and accounting. The consumer figure is partial and the spending forecast is a different metric. One article cannot settle the media-amplification part. The evidence does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'by my estimates', 'more than half' and 'including the hyperscalers'. 'By my estimates' names the source of the estimate; it is not a probability hedge.

contract.note: Comparing contemporaneous annualised rates is a fair plain reading. But the answer depends on the industry boundary and on how reseller and supplier-to-supplier revenue is treated. The speaker supplied neither, so interpretation does decide the result, contrary to the contract's flag.

evidence.note: OpenAI's reported ~$10B annual recurring revenue in June 2025. This is part of the numerator only.
Bloomberg, published Jan 2026 (before the evaluation date): Anthropic's run rate was ~$4B in July 2025. This is part of the numerator only.
Microsoft's $13B AI run rate as of Jan 2025. It is broader than generative AI, earlier than the target period, and may overlap with OpenAI revenue. It is not a comparable denominator.

Epoch's April 2025 analysis says hyperscalers earn more than the top AI labs from reselling models. That points against the claim, but the earlier date and different coverage stop it from settling the July share.

reviews.rationale: The numerator is about $14B annualised in mid-2025. There is no comparable industry-wide generative AI denominator on a consistent basis. The Microsoft and Epoch items suggest hyperscaler revenue is large, but they differ in period and scope and may double-count reseller revenue. The packet does not settle the share.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, stated as his simplified view.

semantics.note: In context, 'relies on' refers to NVIDIA's stock value and growth. Reading it as the valuation depending on sequential sales growth is faithful and fits a causal claim.

contract.note: Using revenue as the measure and requiring evidence of necessity, not mere correlation, is a fair plain reading. No valuation interval is given, which the contract acknowledges.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's CFO commentary shows Q1 FY26 data center compute revenue up 5% sequentially. Revenue rose, so it cannot test what happens to valuation when growth stops.
Reuters: shares rose 3% after hours despite a weak forecast. This is a one-session reaction to guidance, not a test of flat or falling sequential revenue.

reviews.rationale: Neither item shows that NVIDIA's valuation requires uninterrupted sequential GPU revenue growth. Neither shows a sustained valuation through a revenue decline either. The packet does not settle the claimed dependence.

attribution.note: The 'will never exist' clause is Zitron's own assertion. Amodei's warning is only paraphrased as background.

semantics.note: 'Will never exist' is a firm, unbounded forecast. 'Next few years' belongs to Amodei's warning, not to Zitron's deadline. Isolating the embedded forecast from the remark about reporters is reasonable.

contract.note: Reading 'agents' as systems able to replace workers across white-collar roles fits the context. The early-resolution rule needs credible independent demonstration. What counts as 'agents' is supplied by the evaluator, and that choice drives the result.

evidence.note: GDPval shows progress on professional tasks, but with human oversight. It does not show agents taking over whole occupations.
Epoch explains that benchmark scores would not imply end-to-end automation of professions. This limits what benchmark gains can show.
Aug 2026 benchmark finds large completion gaps in real workflows. Finite failures cannot prove 'never'.
A vendor-published anecdote about one recruiter replacing staff, with close supervision and errors. It is not independently verified and not a demonstration across occupations.

reviews.rationale: The 'never' forecast has no deadline. Nothing in the packet meets the early-resolution rule: there is no independently credible demonstration of agents replacing white-collar workers. Current limitations cannot confirm 'never'. The forecast stays open and unresolved.
